en tagrende.explanation: "En tagrende" means "a gutter". It is built from "tag" (roof) and "rende" (channel). To say rainwater runs into it, use "ned i": "Regnvandet løber ned i tagrenden" (The rainwater runs down into the gutter).

en tagterrasse.explanation: "En tagterrasse" means "a roof terrace". To say where you sit or eat, use "på": "Vi spiser på tagterrassen" (We eat on the roof terrace).

en taktik.explanation: "En taktik" means "a tactic". To say a team has a way of playing, use it with the team: "Holdets taktik er at forsvare sig" (The team's tactic is to defend). "En strategi" (a strategy) is the plan for a long time ahead: "Vi har en strategi for de næste fem år" (We have a strategy for the next five years).

en talemåde.explanation: "En talemåde" means "a saying". It is built from "tale" (speech) and "måde" (way). A saying whose words do not mean what they say is "at tage benene på nakken" (to run away fast, literally "to take the legs on the neck").

en tallerken.explanation: "En tallerken" means "a plate". To ask for the kind of plate that holds soup, say "en dyb tallerken" (a deep plate): "Jeg vil gerne have suppe på en dyb tallerken" (I would like soup on a deep plate).

en talsperson.explanation: "En talsperson" means "a spokesperson". To say a man speaks for a group, use "en talsmand" (a spokesman): "Han er foreningens talsmand" (He is the association's spokesman).

en tand.explanation: "En tand" means "a tooth". To say you brush your teeth, use the plural: "Jeg børster tænder" (I brush my teeth). Many words start with it, such as "en tandbørste" (a toothbrush).

en tandbøjle.explanation: "En tandbøjle" means "a dental brace". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "bøjle" (hoop). To say someone wears braces, leave out "en": "Hun har tandbøjle" (She wears braces).

en tandbørste.explanation: "En tandbørste" means "a toothbrush". It is built from "tand" (tooth) and "børste" (brush). To say you brush your teeth, use "at børste tænder" (to brush teeth): "Jeg børster tænder to gange om dagen" (I brush my teeth twice a day).

en tandlæge.explanation: "En tandlæge" means "a dentist". It is built from "en tand" (a tooth) and "en læge" (a doctor). To say you have a dentist visit, use "skal til" (am going to): "Jeg skal til tandlægen" (I am going to the dentist).

en tandlægetid.explanation: "En tandlægetid" means "a dentist appointment". It is built from "tandlæge" (dentist) and "tid" (time or appointment). To say you have no time, use "tid" for time: "Jeg har ikke tid" (I have no time). To say you have an appointment, use "tid" for appointment: "Jeg har en tid klokken ti" (I have an appointment at ten).

en tandplejer.explanation: "En tandplejer" means "a dental hygienist". It is built from "tandpleje" (dental care).

en tang.explanation: "En tang" means "a pair of pliers / seaweed". When you talk about the tool for gripping or cutting wire, use "en tang": "Jeg klipper ledningen over med en tang" (I cut the wire in two with pliers). When you talk about seaweed on the beach, leave out "en": "Der ligger tang på stranden" (There is seaweed on the beach).

en tank.explanation: "En tank" means "a tank". To say what a tank holds, put a word in front: "en vandtank" (a water tank). To say you put fuel in a car, use "på": "Vi fylder benzin på bilens tank" (We put gas in the car's tank).

en tanke.explanation: "En tanke" means "a thought". To thank someone for a kind idea, say "Tak for tanken" (Thanks for the thought). To say you have thought about something, use the plural: "Jeg har gjort mig tanker om det" (I have thought about it).

en tankstation.explanation: "En tankstation" means "a gas station". It is built from "at tanke" (to fill up) and "en station" (a station). To say you need to fill up the car, use the verb alone: "Jeg skal lige tanke" (I just need to fill up the car).

en tante.explanation: "En tante" means "an aunt". To say an aunt is your mother's sister, use "en moster": "Min moster bor i Aarhus" (My mother's sister lives in Aarhus). To say an aunt is your father's sister, use "en faster": "Min faster bor i Odense" (My father's sister lives in Odense).

en tarm.explanation: "En tarm" means "an intestine". To name the parts, put "tyk" (thick) or "tynd" (thin) in front: "en tyktarm" (a large intestine) and "en tyndtarm" (a small intestine).

en tartelet.explanation: "En tartelet" means "a tartlet (vol-au-vent)". In Denmark, the classic filling is chicken and asparagus in sauce: "tarteletter med høns i asparges" (tartlets with chicken in asparagus).

en taske.explanation: "En taske" means "a bag, purse". To name the kind of bag, put a word in front: "en håndtaske" (a handbag) and "en skoletaske" (a school bag). To ask for a plastic shop bag, use "en pose" (a plastic bag): "Må jeg få en pose?" (May I have a bag?)

en tatovering.explanation: "En tatovering" means "a tattoo". It comes from the verb "at tatovere" (to tattoo). To say you will get one, use "få" (get): "Jeg vil have en tatovering" (I want a tattoo).

en tavle.explanation: "En tavle" means "a blackboard". To name another kind of board, put a word in front: "en opslagstavle" (a bulletin board). To say something hangs there: "Der hænger en seddel på opslagstavlen" (A note hangs on the bulletin board).

en tavshed.explanation: "En tavshed" means "a silence". To say someone ended the silence, use "at bryde" (to break): "Han brød tavsheden" (He broke the silence). For quiet with no sound around you, use "stilhed" (quiet): "Der er stilhed i skoven" (It is quiet in the forest).

en taxa.explanation: "En taxa" means "a taxi". To say how you travel, use "med" (by) without an article: "Vi kører med taxa" (We go by taxi). To say you book one, use "at bestille" (to book): "Jeg bestiller en taxa" (I am booking a taxi).

en taxachauffør.explanation: "En taxachauffør" means "a taxi driver". It is built from "en taxa" (a taxi) and "en chauffør" (a driver). To tell the driver where you want to go, say "Til banegården, tak" (To the railway station, please).

en teenager.explanation: "En teenager" means "a teenager". The word comes from English. To say what someone is, leave out "en": "Hun er teenager" (She is a teenager).

en tegnebog.explanation: "En tegnebog" means "a wallet". The word "en pung" also means "a wallet": "Har du din pung?" (Do you have your wallet?)

en tegnefilm.explanation: "En tegnefilm" means "a cartoon". It is built from "at tegne" (to draw) and "en film" (a film). The kind you read is "en tegneserie" (a comic): "Jeg læser en tegneserie" (I am reading a comic).

en tegner.explanation: "En tegner" means "an illustrator". It comes from the verb "at tegne" (to draw). What an illustrator makes is "en tegning" (a drawing): "Tegneren afleverer en tegning i dag" (The illustrator hands in a drawing today).

en tegneserie.explanation: "En tegneserie" means "a comic". It is built from "at tegne" (to draw) and "en serie" (a series). The kind you watch is "en tegnefilm" (a cartoon): "Børnene ser en tegnefilm" (The children are watching a cartoon).

en tegning.explanation: "En tegning" means "a drawing". It comes from the verb "at tegne" (to draw). To say someone draws, use the verb: "Barnet tegner et hus" (The child draws a house).

en tekande.explanation: "En tekande" means "a teapot". It is built from "te" (tea) and "kande" (pot). To say you pour tea, use "hælde op" (to pour): "Jeg hælder te op" (I pour tea).

en teknologi.explanation: "En teknologi" means "a technology". To talk about the field in general, leave out "en": "Han er interesseret i teknologi" (He is interested in technology).

en tekst.explanation: "En tekst" means "a text". To talk about the words of a song, use the same word: "Jeg kender teksten til sangen" (I know the lyrics of the song). To talk about subtitles on a film, put "under" (under) in front: "Filmen har danske undertekster" (The film has Danish subtitles).

en tekstforfatter.explanation: "En tekstforfatter" means "a lyricist / copywriter". When you talk about someone who writes the words for songs, it means "a lyricist": "Han er tekstforfatter for flere sangere" (He is a lyricist for several singers). When you talk about someone who writes ads, it means "a copywriter": "Han er tekstforfatter på et reklamebureau" (He is a copywriter at an advertising agency).

en telefon.explanation: "En telefon" means "a phone". To say mobile phone, use "en mobil": "Jeg har glemt min mobil" (I forgot my mobile phone). To call someone, use "at ringe til" (to call): "Jeg ringer til dig" (I will call you).

en temperatur.explanation: "En temperatur" means "a temperature". To say someone has a fever, use "at have feber" (to have a fever): "Jeg har feber" (I have a fever). To ask how warm it is, say "Hvad er temperaturen?" (What is the temperature?)

en tendens.explanation: "En tendens" means "a trend". To say what something tends to do, add "til" (toward): "en tendens til stress" (a tendency toward stress).

en teori.explanation: "En teori" means "a theory". To say something works on paper but not in real life, use "praksis" (practice): "I teorien virker det, men i praksis gør det ikke" (In theory it works, but in practice it does not).

en tepose.explanation: "En tepose" means "a tea bag". It is built from "te" (tea) and "pose" (bag). To name other bags, put a word in front of "pose": "en indkøbspose" (a shopping bag).

en terapeut.explanation: "En terapeut" means "a therapist". To name the kind, put a word in front: "en fysioterapeut" (a physical therapist). To say you have a visit, use "skal til" (am going to): "Jeg skal til fysioterapeuten" (I am going to the physical therapist).

en termin.explanation: "En termin" means "a due date". When you talk about a baby, it is the day the baby is expected: "Barnets termin er i maj" (The baby's due date is in May). When you talk about a loan, it is the day a payment is due: "Terminen på lånet er den første" (The loan payment is due on the first).

en termokande.explanation: "En termokande" means "a thermos". It is built from "termo" (heat) and "kande" (jug). To say what is in it, put the drink right after: "en termokande kaffe" (a thermos of coffee).

en termokop.explanation: "En termokop" means "a travel mug". It is built from "termo" (heat) and "en kop" (a cup). To say what you bring in it: "Jeg tager kaffe med i min termokop" (I take coffee along in my travel mug).

en terning.explanation: "En terning" means "a die / cube". To say you roll dice in a game, use "at slå med" (to roll): "Jeg slår med terningen" (I roll the die). To say a cube of food, put a word in front: "en bouillonterning" (a bouillon cube).

en terrasse.explanation: "En terrasse" means "a terrace". To say where you sit outside, use "på" (on): "Vi sidder på terrassen" (We sit on the terrace).

en terrorist.explanation: "En terrorist" means "a terrorist". The word for what a terrorist does is "terrorisme" (terrorism): "Politiet bekæmper terrorisme" (The police fight terrorism).

en teske.explanation: "En teske" means "a teaspoon". It is built from "te" (tea) and "ske" (spoon). To give an amount in a recipe, put the food right after: "en teske sukker" (a teaspoon of sugar).

en tid.explanation: "En tid" means "a time". To say how many times something happens, use "en gang" (one time): "Jeg har været der to gange" (I have been there twice). To say an hour, use "en time" (an hour): "Det tager en time" (It takes an hour).

en tid hos lægen.explanation: "En tid hos lægen" means "a doctor's appointment" (literally, "a time at the doctor"). To say a dentist appointment, change the end: "en tid hos tandlægen" (an appointment at the dentist).

en tidsel.explanation: "En tidsel" means "a thistle". To say you remove weeds from a garden, use "at luge" (to weed): "Jeg luger tidsler i haven" (I am weeding thistles in the garden).

en tidsfrist.explanation: "En tidsfrist" means "a time limit". To say you meet it, use "at overholde" (to keep to): "Vi overholder tidsfristen" (We meet the time limit). To say you go past it, use "at overskride" (to exceed): "Han overskrider tidsfristen" (He goes past the time limit).

en tidsplan.explanation: "En tidsplan" means "a schedule". It is built from "tid" (time) and "plan" (plan). To say you keep to it, use "at holde" (to keep): "Vi holder tidsplanen" (We keep to the schedule).

en tidszone.explanation: "En tidszone" means "a time zone". It is built from "tid" (time) and "en zone" (a zone).

en tiger.explanation: "En tiger" means "a tiger". The "g" is not pronounced, so the word sounds like "TEE-uh". To talk about a young tiger, add "unge" (young animal): "en tigerunge" (a tiger cub).

en tigger.explanation: "En tigger" means "a beggar". To say someone begs for money, use the verb "at tigge" (to beg): "Han tigger penge" (He begs for money).

en tilbagebetaling.explanation: "En tilbagebetaling" means "a refund / repayment". When you talk about money a shop gives back, it means "a refund": "Jeg fik en tilbagebetaling for den ødelagte vare" (I got a refund for the broken item). When you talk about paying back a loan, it means "a repayment": "Tilbagebetalingen af lånet starter i januar" (The repayment of the loan starts in January).

en tilbagegang.explanation: "En tilbagegang" means "a decline". To say something is shrinking, use "i tilbagegang" (in decline): "Salget er i tilbagegang" (Sales are declining). The opposite is "en fremgang" (progress): "Der er fremgang i salget" (Sales are improving).

en tilbagemelding.explanation: "En tilbagemelding" means "feedback". To say you will answer later, use it like this: "Jeg giver dig en tilbagemelding i morgen" (I will get back to you tomorrow).

en tilbagevenden.explanation: "En tilbagevenden" means "a return". It comes from the verb "at vende tilbage" (to come back). To say where the return is to, add "til" (to): "tilbagevenden til hjemlandet" (the return to the home country).

en tilbudsavis.explanation: "En tilbudsavis" means "a flyer with offers". It is built from "tilbud" (offer) and "avis" (newspaper). In Denmark, shops deliver these to your mailbox for free.

en tilføjelse.explanation: "En tilføjelse" means "an addition". It comes from the verb "at tilføje" (to add). To say you add a note, use the verb: "Jeg tilføjer en note" (I add a note).

en tilgang.explanation: "En tilgang" means "an approach". To say what the approach is for, add "til" (to): "en tilgang til undervisning" (an approach to teaching).

en tilhænger.explanation: "En tilhænger" means "a supporter". To say you support a sports team, use "en fan" (a fan): "Jeg er fan af FC København" (I am a fan of FC Copenhagen).

en tilhører.explanation: "En tilhører" means "a listener". The same spelling is also the verb "tilhører" (belongs to), from "at tilhøre": "Bogen tilhører mig" (The book belongs to me).

en tilkørsel.explanation: "En tilkørsel" means "an on-ramp". It is built from "til" (to) and "kørsel" (driving). The opposite is "en afkørsel" (an exit): "Tag afkørsel 12" (Take exit 12).

en tilladelse.explanation: "En tilladelse" means "a permission". When you talk about a document that allows something, use "en tilladelse": "en tilladelse til at fiske" (a permit to fish). When you say you need permission, leave out "en": "Du skal have tilladelse" (You need permission).

en tilmelding.explanation: "En tilmelding" means "a registration". To say you sign up, use the verb "at tilmelde sig" (to sign up): "Jeg tilmelder mig kurset" (I sign up for the course).

en tilpasning.explanation: "En tilpasning" means "an adaptation". It comes from the verb "at tilpasse" (to adapt). To say you adapt a plan, use the verb: "Vi tilpasser planen" (We adapt the plan).

en tilskuer.explanation: "En tilskuer" means "a spectator". To say there are many spectators at a match, use the plural: "Der er mange tilskuere til kampen" (There are many spectators at the match).

en tilstand.explanation: "En tilstand" means "a condition". For a country, do not use it; use "en stat" (a state): "Danmark er en stat" (Denmark is a state).

en tilståelse.explanation: "En tilståelse" means "a confession". It comes from the verb "at tilstå" (to confess): "Han tilstod" (He confessed).

en tiltalt.explanation: "En tiltalt" means "a defendant". To say someone is charged with a crime, use "tiltalt for" (charged with): "Han er tiltalt for tyveri" (He is charged with theft).

en tiltrækning.explanation: "En tiltrækning" means "an attraction", as in the pull between two people. For a place tourists visit, use "en seværdighed" (a sight): "Slottet er en seværdighed" (The castle is a sight).

en tilvænning.explanation: "En tilvænning" means "an adjustment". It comes from the phrase "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg vænner mig til byen" (I am getting used to the city).

en time.explanation: "En time" means "an hour". To say when something happens, use "om" (in): "Vi ses om en time" (See you in an hour). When you talk about a lesson or class, it also means that: "Jeg har en dansktime i dag" (I have a Danish lesson today). For time in general, use "tid" (time): "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

en ting.explanation: "En ting" means "a thing". To ask about something you do not recognize, say "Hvad er det for en ting?" (What is that thing?)

en titel.explanation: "En titel" means "a title". When you talk about a book, film or song, it is the name on it: "Hvad er filmens titel?" (What is the title of the film?) When you talk about a rank or job name, it also means that: "Hun har titlen professor" (She has the title of professor).

en titelsang.explanation: "En titelsang" means "a theme song". It is built from "en titel" (a title) and "en sang" (a song). To say you sing along, use "synge med" (sing along): "Jeg synger med på titelsangen" (I sing along to the theme song).

en tjener.explanation: "En tjener" means "a waiter". It comes from the verb "at tjene" (to serve). The same verb also means "to earn": "Hun tjener mange penge" (She earns a lot of money).

en tjeneste.explanation: "En tjeneste" means "a favor / a service". When you ask for help, it means "a favor": "Jeg skylder dig en tjeneste" (I owe you a favor). When you talk about something a company offers, it means "a service": "Banken tilbyder en ny tjeneste" (The bank offers a new service).

en toast.explanation: "En toast" means "a toasted sandwich". To order one, say what is in it: "en toast med ost" (a toasted sandwich with cheese). For plain toasted bread, use "ristet brød" (toasted bread): "Jeg vil have ristet brød til morgenmad" (I want toasted bread for breakfast).

en togbillet.explanation: "En togbillet" means "a train ticket". It is built from "tog" (train) and "billet" (ticket). To name another kind of ticket, put the vehicle first: "en busbillet" (a bus ticket).

en togfører.explanation: "En togfører" means "a train conductor". The person who drives the train is "en lokomotivfører" (a train driver): "Lokomotivføreren kører toget" (The train driver drives the train).

en togrejse.explanation: "En togrejse" means "a train journey". It is built from "tog" (train) and "rejse" (journey). To say you travel by train, use the verb "at rejse" (to travel): "Jeg rejser med tog" (I travel by train).

en togstation.explanation: "En togstation" means "a train station". It is built from "tog" (train) and "station" (station). To say where you are, use "på" (at): "Jeg er på togstationen" (I am at the train station).

en toiletbørste.explanation: "En toiletbørste" means "a toilet brush". It is built from "toilet" (toilet) and "børste" (brush). To say where it stands: "Toiletbørsten står ved siden af toilettet" (The toilet brush stands next to the toilet).

en toldkontrol.explanation: "En toldkontrol" means "a customs check". It is built from "told" (customs) and "kontrol" (check). To say you pass it, use "gå igennem" (go through): "Vi går igennem toldkontrollen" (We go through the customs check).

en tolk.explanation: "En tolk" means "an interpreter". Someone who works with written text is "en oversætter" (a translator): "Oversætteren oversætter bogen" (The translator translates the book).

en tolkning.explanation: "En tolkning" means "an interpretation", as in a reading of a text. When you talk about how an actor plays a role, it also means that: "skuespillerens tolkning af Hamlet" (the actor's interpretation of Hamlet).

en tomat.explanation: "En tomat" means "a tomato". To name food made from tomatoes, put "tomat" in front: "tomatsuppe" (tomato soup) and "tomatsovs" (tomato sauce).

en tombola.explanation: "En tombola" means "a raffle". To say there is a raffle at an event, leave out "en": "Vi har tombola til julefesten" (We have a raffle at the Christmas party). To say you won something in it, use "at vinde" (to win): "Jeg vandt en kage i tombolaen" (I won a cake in the raffle).

en tommelfinger.explanation: "En tommelfinger" means "a thumb". To say your thumb hurts, use "tommelfingeren" (the thumb): "Jeg har ondt i tommelfingeren" (My thumb hurts, literally "I have pain in the thumb"). To say thumbs up, say "tommelfingeren op".

en top.explanation: "En top" means "a top", as in clothing. When you talk about the highest point of something, use the same word: "toppen af bjerget" (the top of the mountain).

en torn.explanation: "En torn" means "a thorn". To say something keeps annoying you, use the saying "en torn i øjet" (literally, a thorn in the eye): "Støjen er en torn i øjet på naboerne" (The noise is a thorn in the neighbors' eye).

en tornado.explanation: "En tornado" means "a tornado". A much larger system of wind and rain is "en orkan" (a hurricane): "Orkanen kom ind over kysten" (The hurricane came in over the coast).

en tortilla.explanation: "En tortilla" means "a tortilla". To say what is inside, use "med" (with): "en tortilla med kylling" (a tortilla with chicken).

en torvehal.explanation: "En torvehal" means "a market hall". It is built from "et torv" (a square) and "en hal" (a hall). In Copenhagen, "Torvehallerne" (the market halls) is a well-known one.

en tradition.explanation: "En tradition" means "a tradition". To say you keep one alive, use "at holde fast i" (to hold on to): "Vi holder fast i traditionen" (We hold on to the tradition).

en tragedie.explanation: "En tragedie" means "a tragedy". When you talk about a play with a sad ending, it also means that: "Hamlet er en tragedie" (Hamlet is a tragedy). The opposite is "en komedie" (a comedy): "Vi så en komedie i går" (We saw a comedy yesterday).
